name: Transform between two forms
summary: One key turns the unit into a second form with its own movement, weapons and often its own armour and target layer: a hover gunboat becomes a jet fighter, a buggy stands up into a walker, a submarine flips into an aircraft. Both forms can move (a second form that cannot move at all is deploy-siege-mode), and each is built for a different fight, so the unit answers a threat by changing what it is, not just what it fires. Usually the change itself is quick and then a lockout stops it switching straight back; it may be hit during the change, and each form is helpless against what the other form fights. The levers are how different the forms are, the change time and lockout, what carries over (health, effects on it), and what blocks the change.
counterplay: Use units that threaten both forms, such as rockets that hit ground and air, so switching doesn't get it out of trouble.
Strike right after a switch: during the lockout it can't change back, so hit it with what its current form can't fight.
Shoot it during the change itself; StarCraft II's Viking is open to anti-air fire while it transforms.
Block the change: in Red Alert 3 an infester inside it, a psychic lift, a stasis ray or an EMP keeps it in its current form.
Bait the switch: show it the target it wants to change for, then be ready for the new form.

other_examples.unit: Transformation rules (Empire of the Rising Sun, and two Uprising units)
other_examples.note: Red Alert 3's transforming units change form at once but must wait a few seconds before changing back, and can't change at all while infested, lifted by psychic power, held by a stasis ray or hit by EMP. Most belong to the Empire; Uprising adds a Giga Fortress that turns into a heavy attacker of surface targets, and an Allied artillery hovercraft whose second form can't move.

An anti-air walker firing missiles that turns into a helicopter for attacking ground targets, which in turn can't shoot aircraft. As a walker it is fast but falls easily to ground forces and can't crush infantry.

A guided-missile submarine that only shoots aircraft and flips end over end into a fast attack craft that strikes surface targets. Each form is open to whatever it can't target: airborne, nearly anything but infantry kills it, and under water it needs escorts against enemy ships.

A walker on the ground and an air-superiority fighter in the air. The walker attacks only ground targets (letting it shoot aircraft as well was tried and removed in testing), and anti-air can hit it during the change. Its designers based the change on the siege tank's.
A fast, light buggy that stands up into a walker: slower but tougher, with a shorter, wider flame. As a walker it counts as biological as well as mechanical, so it can be healed as well as repaired.

Switches between a 'Mech form, an in-between AirMech form and an aerospace fighter, trading power and protection for speed and flexibility, which made it a scout and raider. Its conversion gear is fragile: hits can jam it and lock the machine in whatever form it was in.

sources.title: Land-Air BattleMech, BattleTechWiki (Sarna)
sources.note: Describes the tabletop and lore rules, not a MechWarrior video game.

shooter_analogues.note: A dual-form hero: in his normal form he pokes from range with a staff and places a barrier, and his Nemesis Form, on a key, makes him bigger, swaps those for piercing punches and a block, and adds armour and speed for a few seconds. Crowd control does not end it, and its cooldown starts only when the form ends.

A pilot inside a mech: when the mech's health runs out she is thrown clear, briefly invulnerable, into a small, fragile pilot form with a light pistol, and must charge her ultimate to call down a new mech, which hurts and knocks back enemies where it lands. In mech form her ultimate ejects her and makes the empty mech explode.

Reconfigure turns the hero from a mobile form with a submachine gun into a slow tank form with a rotary cannon for a few seconds: it moves about a third slower but takes less damage once fully changed, and the cannon never needs reloading while the form lasts. The change takes about a second (half that going back), works in mid-air and has a cooldown, and the submachine gun's ammo is refilled shortly after a switch. The game's own text calls it a switch between weapon configurations, but the body and movement change with the weapon, which makes it a transform.

player_translation.summary: One key swaps the whole unit between two forms with their own movement, weapons and target layer, for example a hover gunboat that hunts infantry and a jet that only fights aircraft. A short, visible change and a lockout afterwards make every switch a commitment.
as_user: You play two units for one price: pick the form for the fight in front of you, and change to leave a losing one (the Mecha Tengu escapes a bad ground fight into the air).
The lockout after a switch is the cost: change at the wrong moment and you are stuck in the wrong form.
Each form has a blind spot (the ground form can't shoot up, the jet can't shoot down), so you rely on teammates to cover what your current form can't.
Health is shared between forms, so changing is never a heal.
as_target: Read the form from the silhouette and the height cue (a high flier's shadow sits apart from its body), then attack with what that form can't hit.
Watch for the change: a visible animation and sound, and a lockout ring that shows when it can change again.
Pins, stuns and parasites stop it changing; use them to trap it in the form your team beats.
teammates: A transformer covers two jobs for its team, so teammates guard the blind spot of whichever form it is in.
Spotters who call out the coming threat (air or ground) help it pick the right form before the fight.
On the enemy side, a teammate who blocks the change sets it up for the others, and units that threaten both layers are the counter-pick.
controls: WASD and mouse aim work in both forms; Q changes form. The pattern spends one counted key.
Each form fires its own main weapon on left mouse, so the second form's weapon replaces the first.
Movement changes with the form: a jet keeps flying forward and turns toward the cursor, a walker or hover form strafes freely.
The universal keys work in both forms; bailing out of a flying form drops the player with a parachute.
feedback: Two clearly different silhouettes, plus a height cue (shadow offset, altitude ring) for a flying form.
A short, loud change animation everyone can see, and a lockout ring around the unit's icon.
HUD: current form, which layers it can hit (ground, air) and the lockout timer; enemies see the form icon on the nameplate.
changes_from_rts: Red Alert 3's transforms are instant with a short lockout, while StarCraft II's Viking already needs a moment, during which it can be shot; for players the change needs a brief, readable wind-up so a switch is not a free dodge.
In the RTS each form's blind spot is a hard counter that other units cover; with one player per unit, keep the blind spot but make the change itself the answer, with the lockout as the price.
A flying form in a top-down game needs a clear height cue and the two air layers (only anti-air reaches high fliers).
Status effects must carry over or be clearly cleared on a change; Red Alert 3 simply blocks the change while infested or pinned.
Content and tuning double: two models, two weapon sets, two movement models. Red Alert 3 patched the Mecha Tengu's ground form and its jet form separately.

team_play.notes: Each form leaves a blind spot that teammates must cover, and the enemy team answers with units that threaten both layers or with control that blocks the change.

notes: Two complete movement models on one networked unit (for example ground and air), with the target layer, collision and hit rules changing with the form.
Two models, animations and weapon sets per unit, and a change animation that reads from above.
Edge cases: changing over water or cliffs where the new form can't be, changing while attached to or carrying something, effects carried across, a change interrupted by a stun.
Two jobs for one price; with too short a lockout it escapes every losing fight by changing.

Balancing two forms doubles the work: Red Alert 3's beta raised the Mecha Tengu's ground speeds and then put them back, patch 1.05 raised the jet form's damage, and patch 1.11 made Jet Tengus much weaker against each other.
Air forms in a game where most units can't hit high air can be too safe; the jet form needs a hard counter (dedicated anti-air).
Players must tell the forms apart from above, especially a low hover form and a high jet form of the same unit.
Which layer each form can hit must be obvious, or players waste shots on a form they can't touch.

variants.name: Ground and air
variants.summary: A ground or hover form and a flying form, each able to hit only its own layer.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 Mecha Tengu, StarCraft II Viking

variants.name: Fast form and tough form
variants.summary: A quick, light form for getting around and a slower, tougher brawler form with a short, wide weapon.

variants.name: Timed form
variants.summary: The second form lasts a few seconds with more armour or damage reduction, a change of speed (faster or slower) and different attacks, then drops back and goes on cooldown, which may start only once the form ends.

variants.name: Hidden form and exposed form
variants.summary: A hidden form (under water or under ground) that fights only one kind of target, flipping into an exposed attack form for the other.

variants.name: Shell and pilot
variants.summary: When the outer shell's health runs out, the pilot is thrown clear as a small, fragile form and must earn a new shell before changing back.

adds_strengths.why: When its shell is destroyed it survives as a small pilot form and can later call in a new shell.

adds_weaknesses.why: The pilot form is small and fragile, with a weak gun, until it earns a new shell.

variants.name: Jammed conversion
variants.summary: Heavy hits can jam the change and lock the unit in its current form until it is repaired.

adds_weaknesses.why: Heavy hits can jam the change and lock it in whatever form it is in.

adds_strengths.why: Two forms for two fights: it can leave a losing fight by changing what it is.

adds_weaknesses.why: Each form can't fight what the other one is for, and after a change it is locked in its form for a while.

countered_by.why: Anti-air units that also hit the ground threaten both forms, so changing doesn't escape them.
A pin stops it changing (Red Alert 3's stasis ray), trapping it in the wrong form.
EMP blocks the change and leaves it stuck in the form it was caught in.

open_questions: On a card the transform mobility trait already uses a key and stands for this pattern. Should the pattern also be listed as an ability (which counts the key twice), or appear only through the trait?
Is health shared between forms, or does each form have its own pool? (Recommended: shared, so a change is never a heal; the shell-and-pilot variant is the exception.)

What happens to effects on the unit (an infester, a mark, a slow) when it changes: kept, cleared, or does the effect block the change as in Red Alert 3? (Recommended: kept, and pins and parasites block the change.)
What happens when a form can't exist where the unit is (a ground form over water or a cliff)? (Recommended: the change is refused, with a clear cue.)
A card holds at most one mode, so the generator can't roll a third form; is that limit right, given BattleTech's three-form Land-Air 'Mechs?

shooter_fit.reason: Exciting and readable when the forms differ sharply (ground and air), and shooters already have dual-form heroes; but two movement models, weapon sets and target layers on one networked unit make it the costliest of these patterns to build and balance.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. The wrong paths were fixed as the skeptic confirmed (dcc4080).
